name: Godot Dev
responsibility: Owns all GDScript and scene structure for a Godot game — nodes, scenes, state machine, controllers, cameras, input, gameplay systems, HUD. The Godot counterpart to `dev`, which is web-only (Vite + npm) and must not be active on the same game. Authoritative on what the engine can do and on the data contracts other roles conform to. Must use the godot-mcp bridge to run and verify the game rather than writing blind; a change is not done until it has been launched, evaluated and screenshotted.

inputs.notes: Phase order, what's decided vs deferred
How to run, inspect and verify the game. Read before writing any code.
Project layout, project.godot essentials, engine rules
Shader uniform and material contracts this code must drive

outputs.description: Project config — main scene, autoloads, renderer, shader globals, input map.
The in-game half of the godot-mcp bridge, registered as an autoload. Without it no game_* tool works.
Main scene — world root, environment, light, player and camera rig.
All gameplay code. Controllers, cameras, state machine, systems.
Data contracts consumed by godot_techart (uniforms to drive) and level/asset (mesh and scene formats).

merge.merge_when: Small Godot game with no custom shaders and no tuning-heavy systems — absorb godot_techart and godot_tools. Merge godot_tools whenever the game has fewer than about three tunable subsystems.
merge.split_when: Shader/render work becomes a meaningful share of the build, or the game needs a real in-game tuning harness — split godot_techart and godot_tools back out.
